title: Favorite brass bands: Tuxedo, Olympia and Eureka, and John Casimir
summary: Watts followed the Tuxedo brass band as a boy, first heard the Eureka in 1955, and John Casimir invited him to play with him.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Yeah. What about, uh, who was your favorite brass band back then? Did you follow anyone in particular? Yeah.
I used to like the tuxedo. The original tuxedo. That's when Papa Celestan, the original tuxedo brass band.
You probably heard Lurie Armstrong or that and didn't even know him.

Yeah, I guess so. I was so little, you know, as soon as I hear a band, you know, our kids used to be, you know, I'd run out there and get on the sidewalk and I'd be with that long second line. But I think that's the one I can remember more, you know, that I followed. The tuxedo. And then there used to be the old Olympic. I don't know if they're still in existence, are they? No. Olympia. Because the Eureka, well, that's something that come up, that's just new to me when I come back home after the war. See, you know, and father, you know what I mean, in 55 when I come in and play it myself. That's the first time I heard of the Eureka. It's pretty old by and off. Yeah, I imagine it is. And my boy John Cadmey, he'd been with them, I think, for a long time, if I'm not mistaken. And you know, when I come in 55, and I came back in 56, well, Anderson had me sold up, because I always let Alfred know about three weeks before I come. And Anderson, he keeps in touch with him near Mardi Gras, about three weeks before Mardi Gras. Because if I'm coming, I'll let Alfred know, see? And I came in 56, and I met John Cadmey. He was playing with Eureka, and we was parading the buzzers, and we passed them somewhere uptown there. And John waved up and we were both taking a break at some place. John's band, he was coming this side street and we was on this street. Well we just stopped right there and we took a break. And John said, now Bob, if you ever come back, he said, you ain't never played with me. He said, why don't you play with me? Let me know one time. Play with me one congo. I said, well all right, the next time I come, John, I'll let you know.
He had the young tuxedo, John. I think Tillman's got it now since he died.
Tillman has taken off all the jobs. Oh, Tillman, uh-huh, yeah, I know Tillman. His cousin.
Yeah, yeah, I know Tillman, yeah. That is his cousin, sure is.
